simple.meaning: אַיָּה (ʼayâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “the screamer , i.e. a hawk.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אַיָּה (H344) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 11:14, with occurrences in Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Job.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַיָּה (H344) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אַיָּה (H344) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אַיָּה (ʼayâh) / H344 is traced through Leviticus 11:14, Deuteronomy 14:13, Job 28:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H344. ayyah I. אַיָּה noun feminine hawk, falcon, kite (perhaps from cry; compare Arabic , a kind of hawk) Lev 11:14 ; Deut 14:13 Generic, compare לְמִינָהּ & Di; Job 28:7 (keen-sighted).
